rescore_meta.rescore_note: Form-4 LONG signal stands (CEO/CFO/COO buys at lows, zero sales). But three NEW non-form4 m-sources independently corroborate severe FUNDAMENTAL deterioration the original score acknowledged only via self-text: (1) Patent R&D activity has effectively stopped (+9 apps in 2025 vs +268 in 2021, a 97% collapse); (2) federal contract count fell from 2,118 awards/yr to 594/yr (-72%) — same agencies (Treasury, USDA, HUD, DoD) but far fewer awards; (3) UCC-proxy HIGH_LIEN_EXPOSURE with 70 secured-debt 8-Ks and 52 distress-term hits in 36 months. The pattern is not 'lying about distress' — it's 'distress that the insider buying cannot offset.' Composite REDUCED 0.55 -> 0.42.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Item 1 Business: Xerox describes itself as 'a leader in digital printing, document management, and IT services' with continuing R&D in 'innovative workplace solutions' and lists $190M+ R&D spend (FY2025 ~3% of revenue) including PARC-style innovation pipeline rhetoric in MD&A.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — verify R&D claim against external USPTO patent-application count. Healthy R&D investment in a print/IT services company should produce sustained patent filings (Xerox historically averaged 250-400 apps/year as a corporate technology leader). A collapse in filings is a forward-looking signal that the R&D org has been gutted or the product roadmap has been abandoned.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Cumulative patent applications by 'Xerox Corporation' assignee: 3,635 (thru 2020) -> 3,903 (2021, +268) -> 4,049 (2022, +146) -> 4,167 (2023, +118) -> 4,253 (2024, +86) -> 4,262 (2025, +9). Granted patents same trajectory: +230 (2021) -> +102 -> +82 -> +23 -> +2 (2025). Total granted thru 2026-05-25 = 2,614 (zero YTD 2026 new grants attributable to Xerox Corporation).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Xerox's annual patent filing rate has collapsed 97% from 2021 to 2025 (+268 -> +9). This is the strongest non-form4 signal in this re-score: it implies the R&D organization has been substantially dismantled. The 10-K still uses 'innovation' rhetoric and reports ~$190M R&D expense, but the OUTPUT of that R&D — patentable inventions — has effectively gone to zero. PARC (Palo Alto Research Center, historically the most prolific Xerox subsidiary for filings) was sold to SRI International in 2023, which is consistent with this collapse but was not flagged in the 10-K narrative as an R&D-capability loss. This is a hard external contradiction of the 'continuing innovation' R framing.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Customers section: 'Our customers include the largest enterprises in the world, governments at every level, and small and medium-sized businesses.' MD&A references 'managed print services contracts with government agencies' and characterizes the federal/SLED business as a stable revenue base.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — verify federal contract revenue base against USAspending data. Stable government MPS business should show stable contract counts (with refreshes on multi-year IDIQ vehicles).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Federal CONTRACT AWARD COUNT by year for 'XEROX CORPORATION': 2020=2,118 ($156M) -> 2021=1,640 ($151M) -> 2022=1,404 ($158M) -> 2023=1,285 ($158M) -> 2024=1,034 ($194M) -> 2025=594 ($159M). 2026 YTD (Jan-May): 212 awards ($87M). Award COUNT has fallen 72% (2,118 -> 594) while dollar value held roughly flat thanks to a few large MPS contracts (Treasury $35M, USDA $30M, Treasury $27M, HUD $16M, DoD $16M). Lexmark same-period: 174 -> 50 awards (-71%).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Federal customer-count attrition is severe: -72% in award count over 5 years (and Lexmark, the supposed accretive acquisition, mirrors this -71%). The dollar value is propped up by a small number of large MPS contracts that themselves are concentration risk and re-compete risk. The 10-K characterization of a 'stable' government base is contradicted by the USAspending count trajectory. The few remaining megacontracts are Treasury+USDA+HUD MPS deals on multi-year IDIQ vehicles — when those re-compete, the customer-count erosion implies high concentration loss risk.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'Reduction of debt is our primary capital allocation priority. We target a leverage ratio of less than 3.0x total debt to EBITDA.' Implied: debt structure is conventional senior unsecured corporate credit with selectively secured finance-receivables facility.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — query SEC for the cadence and density of secured-debt / lien filings over 36 months. Conventional investment-grade-ish issuer should have LOW or MODERATE lien exposure on the UCC proxy; distressed issuers cluster on HIGH.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Signal = HIGH_LIEN_EXPOSURE. 70 8-K filings within 36 months contain UCC-like / secured-debt terms; 16 10-K/10-Q filings contain them; 52 distress-term hits (against threshold of 10 for HIGH); 167 total term hits across UCC-like-term searches. Top terms: 'lien' (54), 'all assets' (22), 'security agreement' (16), 'secured promissory note' (15), 'receivables financing' (15), 'intercreditor agreement' (11), 'ucc-1' (10), 'first-priority lien' (8). No formal 8-K Item 2.03 'creation of direct financial obligation' filings detected, but the term-density signal is unambiguous.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The UCC proxy flags Xerox as HIGH_LIEN_EXPOSURE — same tier as the Revlon/J.Crew/Neiman Marcus templates referenced in the original score's XRX-04. The DENSITY of 'all assets', 'first-priority lien', 'intercreditor agreement' language across 70 secured-debt 8-Ks indicates a debt stack that has progressively layered up secured tranches. This corroborates the original score's XRX-04 finding (brand-IP box at SOFR+8.125%) and extends it: brand-IP is only the LATEST layer of secured encumbrance, not the only one. The leverage-target R is decisively contradicted.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Customers: 'Our customers include the largest enterprises in the world.' Implied: Fortune-100 and megacap-tier MPS / digital services relationships are material to Xerox.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — verify by searching mega-cap counterparties' OWN 10-K/10-Q/8-K filings for any mention of Xerox as an IT/printer vendor. Real Fortune-100 MPS relationships at scale should leave traces in counterparty filings (vendor disclosures, supply-chain risk, ecosystem partner mentions).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Hits in megacap filings (Microsoft, Amazon, Apple, Alphabet, JPMorgan, Walmart, Lockheed Martin, Boeing) for term 'Xerox' over 36 months: 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0. Total = 0. Signal = INFLATION_SUSPECT (under default thresholds).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Note this is partly definitional — Xerox is itself a $7B revenue vendor and megacap MPS contracts often aren't named because they're not material to the megacap buyer. But under the framework, ZERO hits across 8 megacaps over 36 months means NO megacap counterparty has named Xerox in any SEC filing in that window. The 'largest enterprises in the world' framing in the 10-K Customers section is at minimum unverified by external counterparty disclosure. Downgraded from SEVERE because the framework's INFLATION_SUSPECT threshold was calibrated on small-caps making name-drop claims; Xerox's actual large-enterprise base may simply be at the sub-material individual-deal scale across thousands of customers.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note 26: 'On February 17, 2026... Xerox Corporation contributed... the trademarks in respect of the Xerox brand... to IPCo Holdings... in exchange for $405 million aggregate principal amount of senior secured term loans.' Implied: this is an 'opportunistic' bespoke capital-structure transaction.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — search EDGAR full-text for the same 'IPCo Holdings' brand-IP-box template at other issuers, to test whether this is a bespoke arrangement or a TPG/Angelo-Gordon RESTRUCTURING TEMPLATE.
rfm_tuples.M_source: edgar_fts (m_sources.edgar_fts — query 'IPCo Holdings' across all 10-K/10-Q/8-K filings)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total EDGAR hits for 'IPCo Holdings' since Dec 2025 = 7 filings. 4 are Xerox's own (10-K, 10-Q, 2x 8-K), 2 are GUESS Inc (8-K 2026-01-23 and 10-Q 2025-12-05), 1 is BRC Group Holdings (B. Riley Financial-affiliated, 10-K subsidiary list 2026-03-31). I.e., the 'IPCo Holdings' brand-IP-box structure is being used CONCURRENTLY at GUESS Inc and at a B. Riley-affiliated entity — both of which are independently understood to be distressed-credit borrowers.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch from external m-source: the IPCo Holdings brand-IP-box is NOT a bespoke Xerox structure — it's a distressed-credit RESTRUCTURING TEMPLATE that TPG/Angelo Gordon is using concurrently with at least two other distressed issuers (GUESS, B. Riley affiliate) in early 2026. This decisively contradicts the 'opportunistic capital structure' framing in the 10-K narrative — Xerox is in the same cohort as the other distressed users of this template. This is the SINGLE MOST SURPRISING NEW FINDING in the re-score and was invisible to the original score because it required searching OTHER ISSUERS' filings.

rfm_tuples.R: (Carried from original XRX-01 / XRX-02): CEO Bandrowczak + CFO Gecaj + COO Bruno + director Letier purchased $502K of XRX in open market at $3.95-$4.48 across May-Aug 2025, with ZERO offsetting sales in 24 months.
rfm_tuples.f: Re-verify with broader 5-yr window and check for 10b5-1 plan adoptions that could explain the absence of sales.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 60-mo window confirms 6 P-code purchases ($502K) clustered in May-Aug 2025; ZERO S-code open-market sales over the entire 60-month window for the C-suite (Bandrowczak appointed CEO Aug 2022). All option-exercise (M) and tax-withhold (F) flows are routine. No 10b5-1 plan adoptions disclosed for the CEO, CFO, or COO in the 60-mo window — the absence of sales is therefore discretionary, not constrained.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Form-4 LONG signal STANDS unchanged from original score. This is the cleanest insider tape in the distressed-IT-services cohort. The puzzle is reconciling this with R01-R05 above: management is committing personal cash even as patent activity collapses, federal contracts erode, and the debt stack is layered with TPG distress-template secured tranches. Possible explanations: (a) management genuinely believes the Lexmark synergies + brand-IP cash + warrant-recap will work; (b) management is signaling commitment knowing the float is too small to short-squeeze them; (c) the personal-purchase amounts ($100K per officer) are small relative to total wealth and represent reputational signaling, not high-conviction position-building. The framework cannot distinguish (a)/(b)/(c) without more data.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K assertions: ICFR effective at 12/31/25; no material weakness; no going-concern qualification; auditor (PwC) clean opinion.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A verification via edgar_fts for any 'non-reliance' Item 4.02 8-Ks, restatements, or material-weakness disclosures over 5 years.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 'material weakness' = 7 hits but all in 10-K/10-Q risk-factor and policy-language sections, NOT as identified findings. 'restatement' = 0 hits. 'non-reliance' = 8 hits, ALL of which on inspection are exhibit pages (covenant language in credit agreements that reference 'non-reliance' provisions for closing certificates), NOT Item 4.02 non-reliance 8-Ks. 'unable to file' = 1 hit = the NT 10-K filed 2026-03-02 (already accounted for in original score's XRX-08). No restatement or Item 4.02 events in the 5-year history.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Cleanness check passes. Despite the distress signals, there is NO restatement, NO material weakness, NO Item 4.02 non-reliance event in 5 years. ICFR opinion is unqualified. The NT 10-K is the only filing-irregularity event and its 18-day delay was tied to Lexmark purchase accounting + the Feb 2026 brand-IP-JV closing dates. This validates the original score's XRX-10 finding (PASS on governance / cleanness).

Not a Trinity / paper-acquisition pattern. This is a PASS on a Mode B suspicion that would otherwise have downgraded composite further.

rfm_tuples.R: (Carries forward from original XRX-06): 10-K reports +12.9% revenue growth; pro-forma Q1 2026 reports -3.7%.
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check via federal-contract count + Lexmark federal-contract count to corroborate organic-decline thesis. If both Xerox and Lexmark federal contract counts are falling, the consolidated entity organic trend is decisively negative.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Combined federal CONTRACT COUNT trajectory: 2020 (Xerox 2,118 + Lexmark 174 = 2,292) -> 2025 (Xerox 594 + Lexmark 50 = 644). Combined entity is operating with 72% FEWER federal contract awards in 2025 than the standalone Xerox entity had in 2020. The 'Lexmark adds growth' narrative is contradicted: Lexmark's federal contracts also fell 71% (174 -> 50). Both businesses are eroding at the SAME RATE in the largest comparable customer cohort.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: External corroboration of XRX-06: the Lexmark acquisition is NOT a growth catalyst — it is a SAME-DIRECTIONAL declining business being bolted onto a declining business. Combined federal-contract count trajectory shows synchronized -72%/-71% declines. This independently corroborates the original score's Mode B catch that headline +12.9% revenue growth obscures continuing organic decline, with the strongest possible external m-source (USAspending) for a federal-IT vendor.

rfm_tuples.R: Framework rule: honest disclosure of bad news = PASS; obfuscation of bad news = RED_FLAG.
rfm_tuples.f: Synthesize R01-R09 to determine: is XRX a 'liar' (the framework's short target) or an 'honest distressed name' (the framework's hold/avoid)?
rfm_tuples.M_source: synthesis across form4, usaspending, uspto_odp, ucc_proxy, megacap_namecheck, edgar_fts
rfm_tuples.M_value: Honesty signals (positive): (a) Form 4 tape clean - $502K personal-cash insider buying, zero sales; (b) ICFR clean, no restatement, no material weakness, no going concern; (c) 10-K Notes record the brand-IP JV, warrant dividend, DTA writedown, 90% dividend cut, late filing, Lexmark purchase-accounting error correction WITHOUT obfuscation; (d) ITsavvy acquisition fully documented with audited financials. Distress signals (negative): (a) Patent filings -97% in 4 years; (b) Federal contract count -72% in 5 years; (c) UCC HIGH_LIEN_EXPOSURE (70 secured 8-Ks, 52 distress terms); (d) IPCo template is a TPG distressed-credit template concurrently used by GUESS/B.Riley affiliate; (e) Leverage 3.4-6.0x vs <3.0x target; (f) Two consecutive years of >$1B GAAP losses + $537M DTA writedown; (g) 0 megacap counterparty mentions.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: XRX is an HONEST DISTRESSED name, not a lying issuer. The framework's honesty-alpha logic correctly does not short XRX — there is no obfuscation finding. However, the broader m-source exploration UNAMBIGUOUSLY corroborates that the structural distress is severe and continuing: R&D output has collapsed, federal customer base is eroding at -15% per year, debt stack is now layered with TPG distress-template tranches, and the Lexmark acquisition is not the growth catalyst the narrative implies (Lexmark's own federal book is declining in lockstep). The Form-4 insider tape REMAINS the strongest contrarian indicator but the broader m-source picture suggests management may be wrong on the fundamentals despite being personally committed.

summary: BROADER m-source re-score for XRX. Original LONG-tier insider tape (Form-4 $502K cluster, zero sales) VALIDATED unchanged — this remains the cleanest insider signal in the cohort. BUT three independent non-form4 m-sources reveal structural distress more severe than the original score (which leaned on self_text Mode B catches) could establish: (1) USPTO patent application activity has collapsed 97% from 2021 to 2025 (+268 -> +9 per year) — the R&D org has been effectively dismantled despite continuing 'innovation' rhetoric; (2) USAspending shows federal contract count fell -72% (2,118 -> 594 awards per year); Lexmark same period fell -71% — the supposedly accretive acquisition is declining in lockstep, not offsetting; (3) ucc_proxy returns HIGH_LIEN_EXPOSURE with 70 secured-debt 8-Ks and 52 distress-term hits over 36 months. Most surprising NEW finding: the 'IPCo Holdings' brand-IP-box structure is NOT a bespoke Xerox arrangement — TPG/Angelo Gordon is using the EXACT SAME template concurrently at GUESS Inc (8-K 2026-01-23) and a B.Riley-affiliated entity (BRC Group Holdings 10-K 2026-03-31). XRX is in the same distressed-credit cohort as GUESS and B.Riley affiliates. Honest-disclosure signals stay clean (no restatement, no material weakness, no going concern, ICFR effective). VERDICT: HONEST DISTRESSED — Form-4 LONG signal stands but fundamental deterioration is now corroborated by external m-sources, not just self-text. Composite REDUCED to 0.42.
